subject: Procurement path check: AWS Marketplace vs PO — next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Megan Stokes <megan.stokes@cloudline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + procurement next steps — Cloudline marketplace/on-prem options

Hi Megan —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can map out the right procurement path (AWS Marketplace vs PO/card vs private offer).

Call highlights:
- Use case: ML inference for clinical insights pipeline (low-latency, bursty queries).
- Preferred deployment: Hosted Redwood API to start; potential Dedicated pool later.
- Security: SOC 2 in place; will need basic vendor answers for procurement.

Open items / asks for procurement team:
1) Payment preference: PO (net 30) or company card? If PO, which legal entity should Redwood invoice?
2) Marketplace interest: are you open to AWS Marketplace (private offer) to simplify invoicing and SaaS billing?
3) Paperwork: do you have a standard vendor form or contract redlines we should expect?
4) Timeline: expected approval window and any quarterly procurement blackout dates?

Attached: Redwood_PO_Template.docx — feel free to use/modify for your finance team.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm payment route (PO vs card) + signing entity
- If Marketplace looks interesting, we can map the private-offer timeline (usually 2–4 wks for setup on the buyer side)
- We’ll loop in Sales Ops (Marissa) for vendor form and SOW logistics

Would you prefer me to introduce Marissa and our finance ops contact directly to your procurement lead?

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0198
https://redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Redwood_PO_Template.docx (docx, 48KB)

From: Megan Stokes <megan.stokes@cloudline.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jacob Lee <j.lee@cloudline.com>, procurement@cloudline.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + procurement next steps — Cloudline marketplace/on-prem options

Thanks, Dylan — great summary. Quick answers from procurement side: 

- We’d prefer a PO (net 30) if possible — finance team requires it for vendor spend above $25k.
- We are open to exploring AWS Marketplace private offers to keep billing consolidated with our cloud spend team, but we need to confirm with FinOps.
- I’ll share our vendor form and standard redlines; Jacob (cc’d) owns vendor onboarding.
- Timeline: assuming vendor form + legal review, likely 3–5 weeks unless there are contract redlines.

Two quick clarifying Qs:
1) If we go Marketplace private offer, does Redwood still provide the same SLA/entitlements as direct invoicing?
2) Any issues with our standard data-processing appendix?

I’ll attach the vendor intake worksheet in a follow-up from procurement.

— Megan
Megan Stokes
Senior Procurement Manager | Cloudline Therapeutics
megan.stokes@cloudline.com | +1 (617) 555-4482

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Megan Stokes <megan.stokes@cloudline.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + procurement next steps — Cloudline marketplace/on-prem options

Megan — thanks, that helps. Answers below and a couple of operational notes.

1) SLA / entitlements: Yes — private offers via AWS Marketplace preserve the agreed commercial terms; for some enterprise features (dedicated pools, private deployments) we still maintain a separate SOW that references the same SLAs. We can include the SLA clause in the Marketplace listing or in the accompanying SOW (your preference).

2) Data-processing appendix: Redwood has a standard DPA we can attach; if Cloudline has amendments we can review. Karthik (cc) will share the DPA + SOC 2 summary.

Operational items:
- Attached: Redwood_AWS_PrivateOffer_Process.pdf (high level timeline + steps) and Redwood_PO_Template.docx (same as earlier).
- For Private Offer: buyer-side steps typically: accept private offer + procurement confirmation in AWS Console -> payment consolidated to AWS invoice. Onboarding for the buyer typically takes ~2–3 weeks once finance signs off.
- If you want direct invoice (PO), we’ll issue monthly invoices to the legal entity you provide; net-30 terms are supported.

Next steps I propose:
- Jacob / procurement to send vendor intake (we’ll fill/respond to the form)
- Karthik to share DPA and SOC 2 snapshot (today)
- Marissa to coordinate SOW and sign route (DocuSign or Marketplace private-offer)

If you’re ok, I’ll introduce Marissa and our finance ops contact directly to Jacob.

Best,
Dylan

Attachments: Redwood_AWS_PrivateOffer_Process.pdf (pdf, 112KB); Redwood_PO_Template.docx (docx, 48KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jacob Lee <j.lee@cloudline.com>, procurement@cloudline.com
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Recap + procurement next steps — Cloudline marketplace/on-prem options

Forwarding to Jacob / procurement team — hi all, I’m Marissa (Sales Ops) and I’ll handle the paperwork and SOW routing on Redwood’s side. Quick checklist to speed things up: 

- Please complete our vendor intake form: https://redwoodinference.com/vendor-intake (or attach your own)
- If using PO: send the PO to billing@redwoodinference.com and include legal entity + tax ID; we’ll generate invoices monthly.
- If using AWS Marketplace private offer: share the AWS account ID(s) used for purchasing so we can configure the private offer.
- If you prefer DocuSign for the SOW, here’s the envelope: https://docusign.net/envelope/ABC123xyz — I can re-send the SOW with Cloudline fields pre-filled.

Attached: Cloudline_SOW_v1.docx (docx, 72KB) — draft SOW for hosted Redwood API.

Low-friction route recommendation (if you want the fastest path to production): accept a private offer on AWS (less vendor paperwork for finance) + we attach the SOW in DocuSign for signature within the same week. If procurement prefers PO, we’ll accept that route but timeline often depends on internal finance cycles.

Jacob / team — can you confirm preferred route and share the procurement contact + any third-party vendor-form instructions?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0246
